title: Scan four groceries across a checkout scanner, one read each, and put them on the bagging shelf
instruction: Ring up the four groceries on the scanner, each item read once, and put them on the bagging shelf.
context: Cashiers (O*NET 41-2011.00; 3.1 million US jobs, 2025) "Establish or identify prices of goods, services, or admission, and tabulate bills, using calculators, cash registers, or optical price scanners". At a bioptic scanner such as Zebra's MP7000 each item is passed with its barcode toward a window and no finger over it; the scanner beeps and flashes its green LED on each read, and once the barcode has been out of view for 0.5 s (Zebra's default same-symbol timeout) a second pass rings the item up again. An item bagged unread leaves unpaid. Here every barcode starts facing away from both windows, and the belt and the bagging shelf are farther apart than one arm reaches, so items go from hand to hand across the scanner.
setup: A checkout counter (the table top) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the counter. (1) Scanner, fixed: a Zebra MP7000 short in-counter bioptic scanner, 35.1 cm along y by 29.2 cm along x (x 2 to 31.2, y -2.3 to 32.9), its platter flush with the counter; horizontal sapphire window 15 x 10 cm (x 9 to 19, y 7.8 to 22.8); a tower 12.8 cm tall at x 23.7 to 31.2 with the vertical window (22 x 9.2 cm, y 4.3 to 26.3, 1.8 to 11 cm up) on its front face, facing the robot; the LED on the tower's right end, dim green when ready, flashing bright green on each read. (2) Belt end, fixed: black rubber flush with the counter, x 2 to 40, y 45.5 to 64.5. (3) Groceries, loose, on the belt, each with a 12-digit UPC-A barcode (100 % size, bars upright) on one side, none facing a window: a 1 lb spaghetti box (26.4 x 7.1 x 4.1 cm, 0.48 kg) lying along x at (20, 49), its code on its left face 7 cm from its middle away from the robot; a 10.75 oz can of condensed soup (6.8 x 10.2 cm, 0.35 kg) standing at (4.5, 60.5), code facing back toward the robot; a 16 oz glass jar of salsa (7.5 x 12.7 cm, 0.65 kg) at (15, 60.5), code facing left; a 16.9 fl oz bottle of water (6.5 x 20.4 cm, 0.52 kg) at (26, 60.5), code facing left. (4) Bagging shelf, fixed: brushed stainless flush with the counter, x -5 to 40, y -64.5 to -46, its inner edge marked by a yellow line. The right gripper reaches no further left than y 45 and the left gripper no further right than y -45. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step (20 Hz) the task file reads each grocery's pose and both arms' joints. A code is read when its centre is within 15 cm of a window (over or in front of the glass, up to 2 cm past its edge), it faces that window within 45 degrees, it moves slower than 1.5 m/s, and no part of either arm (links, gripper, fingers) lies between the window and any of nine points over the code; the LED then flashes for 0.5 s. After a read the same code reads again only once it has been out of view for 0.5 s (the MP7000's default). Score: 0 for the rest of the run once the glass jar falls faster than 1 m/s (dropped about 5 cm) or tumbles faster than 5 rad/s (knocked over), or any grocery falls off the counter. Otherwise 0.25 per item checked out: read exactly once and ending on the bagging shelf (its whole footprint past the yellow line, resting on the shelf, moved less than 3 mm in the last 1 s, every finger 2 cm or more from it). An item read but left on the counter, or read twice or more, earns nothing; an item that reaches the shelf before its first read scores 0 for the rest of the run (it left unpaid). Full score (1.0, success): all four checked out, held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the scanner's beeps and its decode log on the POS (or Zebra's 123Scan) give each item's reads; a photo of the shelf gives the bagged items; the videos show a drop.
reset_notes: Stand or lay the four groceries back on their taped marks on the belt with their barcodes turned as in the screenshot; void the transaction on the POS. Nothing is consumed. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz; everything at true size. The scanner is not simulated optically: a read is computed from the code's pose (range, facing, speed, line of sight past the arms) with Zebra's 0.5 s same-symbol timeout; the real MP7000 also reads some codes at steeper angles. The bars are drawn at true size but not decoded during the run (OpenCV decodes the drawn labels). The LED flash is modelled, the beep is not. Labels are visual only. No third-party assets.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left arm went to the water bottle and knocked it over onto the counter, then hovered over the jar, the can and the scanner's tower while the right arm stayed near its base; nothing was read and nothing reached the shelf); demo: 1.0
